recipes.name: Chicken with Green Peppers in Black Bean Sauce
ingredients_raw: 4 cloves garlic cloves, peeled and sliced
0.75 pound skinless, boneless chicken breast half - cut into cubes

steps.text: Heat a wok over a medium heat until hot, add the toasted sesame oil and heat for about 30 seconds. Stir in garlic and black bean sauce, and season with salt. Add chicken to the wok; cook, stirring frequently, until chicken is cooked through. Pour in dissolved chicken bouillon, cover, and cook for 6 minutes.

Stir in onion, green onions, and bell pepper, and season with soy sauce and black pepper. Cover, and cook for 8 minutes. Stir in cornstarch mixture, and stir until sauce thickens. Stir in cilantro, and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken with Green Peppers in Black Bean Sauce
raw_recipe.description: A flavorful black bean sauce is the base for this simple and classic dish.

review.reviewBody: This dish is delicious! A note for first-time makers: when making the cornstarch & water mixture to thicken the sauce, don't add the cornstarch to HOT water or you will end up with a dish full of glue. Add it to cold water and then stir in to thicken the sauce. This may be common knowledge for some but it wasn't for me!

As good or even better then the local restaurant. Used boneless/skinless thighs (marinate for 10 mins with 1 tbps sake, pinch of white pepper and kosher salt). Couldn't find plain black bean sauce so we used AMOY Black Bean & Garlic Sauce and reduced to 1 minced clove of garlic. Only used 2 tbps of Sauce, omitted extra salt and the soy sauce. Used half cup of regular chicken stock in place of bouillon. Also threw in a bunch of enoki mushrooms. For the cornstarch slurry at the end, mixed it first into a bit of cold chicken stock, before stirring in with green onions. Great over steamed rice or rice noodles!

I do a lot of Sichuam mala (麻辣) style cooking. This recipe is a pretty good but bastardized version of mala cooking. I was nearly finished writing a detailed explanation for how to cook this properly, but this website kicked me out in order to refresh itself. For that reason, I'm no longer going to give you a full explanation, but, in short, begin by marinading the chicken cubes in Shaoxing rice wine and bean sauce. Combine vegetable oil with the sesame seed oil, to conserve your more expensive sesame seed oil, as many Chinese do. Then fry some crushed sichuan pepper, and follow the rest of the recipe, but cut down on the bean sauce (豆瓣酱), add sweet noodle sauce (甜面酱) and fermented black beans, and use chicken stock. Refrain from using any salt or soy sauce. If you’re a purist, substitute leeks for the green onions. No cilantro! I love cilantro, but it doesn’t belong in this dish. Serve with white rice and some soup dumplings (小笼包). Serve the dumplings with a small dish, consisting of soy sauce and rice or cane vinegar and a dollop of spicy chili crisp, for dipping.
I made but no added salt. Sesame oil not for frying! It's a finishing oil, drizzle on dish at end. Black bean sauce salty. Add sugar, and for stock I use no added salt stock pots.

I will rate only 3 stars because as is, it's too salty, almost inedible. I LOVED what I did though, but here are the changes I made:
- 4 TBS Black Bean sauce (insted of 6!!)
- No additional salt
- No Chicken bouillon, just unsalted chicken stock
- After adding the veggies, just cook for 5 more min (8 is way too much)
- 3 Tsp Cornstarch (insted of 4)

I'm Extremely excited, This is definitely going into the the recipe Box. This easy to make Dinner meal took less than 30 minutes to prepare and make. The recipe was very easy to follow and the ingredients were not hard to find. After taking the advice of several reviewers, this turned out to be a great dining experience. my advise is to go easy on all the salt additives like Soy sauce, chicken bullion, Note; I only used 3 Tbsp. of the Black bean sauce, not the recommended 6 Tbsp. also I used only half of the amount of cornstarch to help thicken the sauce. I added 1 can of mushrooms and 1 can of waterchestnuts. I will be making this recipe again very soon. Thank you
Sam
Chino,Ca.

Okay, the secret to toning down the saltiness of this dish is to omit the salt, chicken bouillon, and the soy sauce. Then increase the water to 1 cup. Use 1 1/2 Tablespoons (4 1/2 teaspoons) cornstarch dissolved in 1/4 cup additional water to thicken. Also, stir in 1 teaspoon sugar. Without so much salt, this is delicious.

This was great. Skipped the salt, used low sodium soy sauce and a little chicken broth rather than the bouillon and it was not too salty at all. Added a splash of Sriacha and tons of different veggies. Thanks for sharing!

This was really good but I did what a lot of the others did with regard to the saltiness. I only used 3 tbsp of the black bean sauce, no salt, no soy sauce, and just a bit of the broth mixed with a lot of water. I also doubled the amount of the chicken. My family and I loved it. I will definitely make it again.

Very simple to make & very tasty. I marinated the chicken in the black bean sauce & garlic before stirfrying the chicken in the sesame oil. The black bean sauce is pretty salty...I didn't need to add any additional salt, or the soy sauce. I did add some pre-sauted mushrooms & zucchini, as well as some black bean tofu, which really worked in this dish. Didn't need to do the cornstarch...the sauce was thick enough. Will definitely make again!

Fabulous recipe. Served it at an ethnic dinner club and received several thumbs up. Few small adjustments; substituted 1-2 Tbsp HOT black bean sauce for some regular for more spice, used chicken broth vs. bouillon. I found the bean sauce salty so cut out the salt and used light (vs. dark) soy sauce. Not sure exactly where to find or what to do for 'toasted' seasame oil so used regular seasame oil heated in toaster oven. I'm always nervous to make a recipe for the 1st time for a big groug but it worked great & pretty easy to prepare.

Because of high sodium content in black bean sauce I did not add additional salt. I put a splash of dark soy on my individual serving. To me, it's reminiscent of chop suey! I would make this again and add a stalk of chopped celery to compliment the flavor.
The dish was just HEAVENLY!
Not my type of dish it does not satisfy my palete taste, I was so frustrated of the outcome. : (
I liked it but next time I won’t add salt.
This was a stable in my house growing up. My dad use to marinate the raw chicken in mixture of cornstarch and soy sauce which made the chicken very tender, eliminating the corn starch in the recipe.

Added some sweet ( ketjap manis) soy sauce and some small bottom mushrooms.
Very nice will make it again.
Cut to 2T black bean sauce, no salt. Add tsp. Sugar. 1 whole onion, green onions. Add mizuna last.

Most people has same comment, the chicken came out bit salty. I would not add any additional salt apart from salt content in black bean sauce.

Apart from salt taste dish is delicious!
Great recipe xxxr
